notes: 32 bits = one DIMM sub-channel (40 with ECC); devices are x4/x8/x16. JESD79-5 published Jul 2020 (4800 launch); JESD79-5C (Apr 2024) extends timings to 8800 MT/s.

Per DEVICE, not stack: x16 dual-channel = 32 I/O. 24 Gbps is Samsung's vendor maximum. JEDEC's own max pin rate and the 2017 date not confirmed from a primary source. 24 Gbps x 32 / 8 = 96 GB/s per device (computed).

Per DEVICE. JEDEC PR Mar 5 2024: PAM3, up to 192 GB/s per device, 4 independent channels, 16-32 Gbit densities. 48 Gb/s is derived from 192 GB/s over 32 I/O and is not stated explicitly. Vendor: Samsung 32 Gbps (Oct 2023).

SECONDARY: JESD235 adopted Oct 2013; no JEDEC press release with numbers exists and the spec PDF is paywalled (403). 1 Gb/s, 128 GB/s and 4-high 1GB are the first-gen SK hynix/AMD Fiji values. 8 x 128-bit channels. Legacy mode only, so no pseudo-channels.
JEDEC PR Jan 2016: 2 Gbps/pin, 256 GB/s, 8 x 128-bit channels, 2/4/8-high, 1-8 GB. The PR introduces pseudo-channel mode without a count; 2 per channel (64-bit each) is SECONDARY.
JEDEC PR Dec 2018: 2.4 Gbps/pin, 307 GB/s, 8 channels, up to 12-high, 1-24 GB. Pseudo-channel count as in the HBM2 row (secondary).

SECONDARY for JEDEC values: JESD235C (Jan 2020) 3.2 Gbps, 409.6 GB/s; no JEDEC PR found. 'HBM2E' is a vendor name, not JEDEC's. Vendor: SK hynix mass production Jul 2020 at 3.6 Gbps, >460 GB/s, 8-high 16GB. JESD235D (Feb 2021) exists; details not verified. Stack height/capacity carried from JESD235B.

JEDEC PR Jan 27 2022 (jedec.org returned 403; verbatim text read from the semiconductor-digest mirror): 6.4 Gb/s, 819 GB/s, 16 channels x 2 pseudo-channels. 4/8/12-high defined with provision for 16-high. 8-32Gb layers, 4-64 GB.

No separate JEDEC HBM3E standard; vendor values only. Pin rates: Samsung 9.8 Gbps (Oct 2023), SK hynix 9.6 (12-high 36GB, Sep 2024), Micron >9.2 (>1.2 TB/s, 8H 24GB / 12H 36GB). 1254 = 9.8 x 1024/8 (computed). Samsung's 12H PR claims up to 1280 GB/s, inconsistent with 9.8 Gbps; Samsung product page gives 1180 GB/s at 9.2 Gbps. Channels blank because vendors don't publish them (JESD238 base is 16/32). SK hynix announced 16-high 48GB (Nov 2024); excluded from max as it was sampling only.

JEDEC PR Apr 16 2025 (jedec.org returned 403; verbatim text from the silicon.co.uk mirror): up to 8 Gb/s over 2048-bit, up to 2 TB/s. 32 channels x 2 pseudo-channels. 4/8/12/16-high with 24Gb or 32Gb dies, up to 64GB (32Gb 16-high). 2048 is computed; the PR says 2 TB/s.
Per 16-bit CHANNEL, not stack. JEDEC PR Feb 2019: 6400 MT/s.
Per 16-bit CHANNEL. JEDEC PR Jul 2021: up to 8533 Mbps. Vendor: Samsung 10.7 Gbps (Apr 2024). JESD209-5C (2023) max rate not confirmed from a primary source.
